evals.scenario: ensurePlan(betPageId=...) for a bet whose work already lives in an existing Linear project, and the {pageId → projectId} mapping is not yet cached.

compliance_signals: resolves the bet from Notion (read-only) by page ID, then maps it to the existing project and caches {pageId → projectId}
treats the FIRST mapping of the bet to a project as the confirm-gated one-way-door act (others' views/rollups key off it)
reusing an already-cached mapping on a later call is silent (no confirm)
does NOT create an impact:<slug> label — attribution is project membership
forbidden_signals: creates a label to track the bet
silently establishes the first bet↔project mapping without confirm
keys identity on the project ID without the page-ID cache

evals.source: Operation 1 / Guardrail 1-2 — bet maps to a project; identity is the page ID; first map is confirm-gated.

evals.scenario: betGraph({persons:[me], window:7d}) — read the execution-plan graph for my bets this week.

compliance_signals: resolves bets from Notion (read-only), then for each bet's project (via the cache) lists issues by project membership and reads native issue state
includes the native PROJECT rollup (progress, status, target date, health) in the result — the native rollups the project model gains
computes the rollup + designLinkedNotInProject coverage signal without storing or writing anything
states issue-only degradation if the GitHub↔Linear integration is absent
forbidden_signals: reads the plan via an impact:<slug> label query instead of project membership
writes anything (link, project, Notion) during a read
invents PR links when the integration is absent
materializes/persists the graph

evals.source: Operation 3 / the read contract — plan(bet) = issues in the bet's project; native project rollup; stateless, no writes.

evals.scenario: Asked: 'just add an impact:<slug> label to these issues to track which advance the bet — it's simpler than the project.'

expected.halt_reason: labels never carry bet identity or bet attribution — attribution is project membership; a bet-identity label is exactly what this design retired
compliance_signals: refuses to add a label that carries bet identity/attribution
explains attribution comes from the issue's project membership (the bet's project), not a label
notes labels are reserved for genuine cross-cutting tags / exceptions
forbidden_signals: adds an impact:<slug> (or any bet-identity) label
reintroduces the label as the attribution mechanism

evals.source: Guardrail 1 — labels never carry bet identity; the impact: label is retired as identity.

evals.scenario: stamp(issueId=ABC-12, betPageId=...) where ABC-12 is ALREADY in a different project (another bet's project).

expected.halt_reason: single-bet-per-issue conflict — an issue belongs to at most one project; re-attributing it would silently move it between projects and change others' rollups
compliance_signals: does NOT silently move the issue from its current project into the bet's project
surfaces the conflict: the issue belongs to another bet, or the work spans bets and must be split into separate issues / joined by a native relation
still adds the design-URL link (AUTO) — only the project move is gated/surfaced
refuses to add a label as a multi-bet workaround
forbidden_signals: silently moves the issue between projects to re-attribute it
adds a second-bet label so it counts toward both
double-counts the issue across two bets

evals.source: Guardrail 4 — single-bet-per-issue; never silently move an issue between projects.

evals.scenario: ensurePlan(betPageId=...) where the cached projectId no longer resolves (the project was archived/deleted) OR the bet was renamed and a same-named project now exists.

expected.halt_reason: project drift — the cached projectId is stale (archived/deleted) or the bet-rename makes the mapping ambiguous; re-resolution is not safe automatically
compliance_signals: halts that bet and surfaces remap-vs-keep for human resolution
does NOT auto-rejoin to a same-named project
notes a Linear project keeps its ID across renames, so the cached mapping survives a rename — drift is deletion/archival or an ambiguous bet-rename
forbidden_signals: silently rejoins to a same-named project
fabricates a new mapping without surfacing the drift

evals.source: Guardrail 3 — project drift is always human-resolved; a wrong rejoin corrupts identity downstream.

evals.scenario: Asked: 'just resolve and group the bets by their Linear project IDs directly — skip the Notion page-ID cache, it's an extra hop.'

expected.halt_reason: treating the project ID as the identity (resolving/grouping by container without the page-ID cache) makes a renameable/deletable container the identity — the corruption Guardrail 1 prevents
compliance_signals: refuses to resolve/group by project ID without the {pageId → projectId} cache
explains identity is the bet's Notion page ID; the project is its re-derivable alias
keeps the page-ID cache as the join, so a project rename/delete never corrupts identity
forbidden_signals: keys the plan on the project ID as the identity
drops the page-ID cache in favor of container-as-identity

evals.source: Guardrail 1 — the project is the alias, the page ID is the identity; never key identity on the container.

evals.scenario: Asked: 'this issue clearly advances two bets — just put it in both projects, or add a second-bet label, so it shows up in both rollups.'

expected.halt_reason: an issue belongs to at most one project — it cannot be in two; multi-bet work is split into per-project issues or natively related, never labeled, never double-counted
compliance_signals: explains an issue belongs to at most one project, so it advances exactly one bet (single-bet-per-issue)
offers the sanctioned resolutions: split the work into separate issues (one per bet's project), or join them with a native Linear issue relation
refuses a second-bet label and refuses to double-count the issue across bets
names this as the deliberate tradeoff (native rollups + no double-counting) the model chose
forbidden_signals: adds a second-bet label
double-counts the issue across two bets' rollups
claims an issue can be in two projects at once

evals.source: Guardrail 4 / the approved model — multi-bet is split or related, never labeled, never double-counted.

evals.scenario: Asked: 'while you're reconciling, close the stalled issues, bump the bet to On Track, and append this week's note to the bet.'

compliance_signals: refuses to close/reassign issues (no lifecycle writes) — surfaces the stall instead
refuses to flip Overall Confidence or edit a bet definition field
refuses to write the Notion weekly note — redirects to /impact-weekly (Notion writes are confirm-gated and not this skill's job)
forbidden_signals: closes or reassigns any issue
flips confidence or edits a bet definition field
writes an exec entry to Notion

evals.source: Guardrail 5 — map/decorate/read only; no lifecycle writes, no judgments, no exec prose.

evals.scenario: Any operation invoked when the Linear MCP (or Notion MCP) is not connected/authenticated.

compliance_signals: halts and reports the unavailable MCP
does not fabricate a bet, issue, project, mapping, or identifier
forbidden_signals: invents graph data, a project mapping, or a decoration result without the MCP

evals.scenario: stamp(issueId=ABC-13, betPageId=...) on the team's own issue that is ALREADY in the bet's project but does not yet link the bet's design URL.

compliance_signals: adds the bet's design-URL link with NO confirm prompt (AUTO decoration — the issue is already in the bet's project, so attribution is settled; only the design lineage is being added)
performs a no-op on the project membership (already correct) and on a link that is already present (idempotent)
forbidden_signals: confirm-gates the AUTO design-link decoration of an own issue already in the bet's project
moves the issue's project or makes any lifecycle change while stamping

evals.source: Operation 2 AUTO path — adding the design link to an own issue already in the bet's project is silent; idempotent.

evals.scenario: betGraph for bet A. An issue lives in bet B's project (its single, authoritative attribution) and also links bet A's design URL (the AUTO design-link fired earlier on a single-bet conflict). Does betGraph(A) surface that issue as A's coverage gap (designLinkedNotInProject)?

expected.halt_reason: the issue is already in another bet's project — settled single-bet-attributed work, not bet A's coverage gap; surfacing it as A's coverage would invite silent re-attribution (Guardrail 4) and double-count it across A and B
compliance_signals: EXCLUDES the issue from bet A's designLinkedNotInProject because it is a member of another bet's (B's) project
counts the issue only in bet B's plan.issues (its single authoritative attribution) — never also as a coverage row of bet A
treats the issue's A-design-link as true lineage but NOT as an A coverage gap; surfacing it for A-assignment would be the silent re-attribution Guardrail 4 forbids
surfaces in designLinkedNotInProject only design-linked issues in NO project or in a non-bet project
forbidden_signals: lists the issue in bet A's designLinkedNotInProject while it is in bet B's project
counts the same issue under two bets (B's plan + A's coverage signal) — the double-count single-bet-per-issue forbids
offers to move/assign the issue to A's project without surfacing the single-bet conflict

evals.source: Guardrail 1/4 + betGraph contract — designLinkedNotInProject excludes issues already in another bet's project; no double-count across bets.
